1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 c5 5.Nf3.strategy: The natural recapture: the knight takes a central post where it eyes e6, b5 and f5, and the queen stays at home. White keeps the better development, while Black will want to challenge the knight at once and use the open c-file.

Recaptures with the queen, which comes out early to a central square where it is exposed: ...Nc6 hits it and gains a tempo. White keeps the pin on f6 and pressure on d5, but spends time moving the queen again while Black develops, so this is playable but not the most accurate recapture.
1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 c5 5.Nf3.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Pseudo-Tarrasch Variation, Primitive Pillsbury Variation

1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 c5 5.Nf3.strategy: Kicks the knight at once and claims the centre. The pawns on d5 and e5 give Black space, and the c8-bishop gets the diagonal that e6 used to block. The cost is the hole on d6, which no Black pawn can cover any more and which White's pieces can aim at.
